meta.description: Design tasks for three major features: (1) platform feasibility detection during setup, (2) flow failure feedback loop back to setup, (3) inline tab-based human approval layer with tone learning.

tasks.title: Platform constraint registry
tasks.description: Create a static registry of known automation constraints per platform. Used by the flow planner to flag or exclude infeasible flows before build time.

details.format: A JSON/TS object keyed by platform domain pattern

constraints.reason: Reddit Chat UI (rs-app, rs-rooms-nav) is built with nested Web Components behind multiple Shadow DOM layers. Standard document.querySelector cannot pierce these boundaries. All DM content is unreachable via CSS selectors.
constraints.workaround: None via DOM. Reddit's Sendbird API could theoretically be called directly but requires session token extraction.

constraints.reason: Reddit detects rapid automated interactions. Posting too frequently triggers shadowbans.
constraints.workaround: Space actions with wait_ms, randomise intervals, cap per-subreddit frequency.

tasks.title: Inject platform constraints into planFlows system prompt
tasks.description: When planning flows during agent setup, detect the target platform from the agent's system prompt / user description, look up constraints, and inject them into the planner's context so it never proposes infeasible flows.

logic: Extract platform signals from systemPrompt + description (regex + keyword match on domain names)
Look up matching constraints from the registry
Append a PLATFORM CONSTRAINTS block to the planner system prompt
Instruct the planner: do not propose flows that are marked blocking, do flag rate_limit constraints in the flow description
details.prompt_block_example:
PLATFORM CONSTRAINTS for reddit.com:
- Direct messages (DMs): BLOCKED — Reddit Chat uses nested Shadow DOM (Web Components), CSS selectors cannot reach it. Do NOT propose any DM or chat flows.
- Rate limiting: space comment/post actions, never batch more than 3 per hour per subreddit.
details.output: Planner only surfaces feasible flows. Blocking constraints are silently excluded. Rate-limit constraints appear as notes in flow descriptions.

tasks.title: Show platform constraint summary in flow planning UI
tasks.description: In the flow planning phase of the setup wizard, display a small 'platform notes' block above the proposed flows list that tells the user what was automatically excluded and why.

details.ui: A collapsible amber/yellow notice block above the flow list. Title: 'Platform notes for [platform]'. Lists blocking constraints with plain-language explanations. Example: '⚠ Reddit DMs are not automatable (Shadow DOM) — DM flows were excluded from this plan.'
details.behaviour: If no constraints apply, block is not shown. If constraints exist, block is shown collapsed by default, expandable.

tasks.title: Feasibility note on individual flows in the generator
tasks.description: When the flow generator is building a flow and encounters a constraint mid-build (e.g. a selector fails consistently for Shadow DOM reasons), it should recognise the pattern, explain the platform-level cause, and offer to mark the flow as infeasible rather than keep trying technical workarounds.

details.addition: Add a PLATFORM FEASIBILITY section to the generator system prompt: 'If you encounter repeated selector failures on a known Shadow DOM site, stop attempting technical solutions. Explain the Shadow DOM constraint clearly, tell the user this flow is not automatable via the browser extension, and offer to mark it as infeasible so the agent setup can adjust its scope.'
details.ui_hook: FlowGenerator should support an onInfeasible callback alongside onFlow. When called, AgentOnboarding treats it the same as skip but records the reason.

tasks.title: Mark flow as infeasible
tasks.description: Add an 'infeasible' status to flows with a required reason field. Infeasible flows are kept for audit purposes but excluded from the agent's tool list.

details.schema_change: ADD COLUMN infeasible INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, ADD COLUMN infeasible_reason TEXT
details.ui: FlowEditor + FlowsTab get a 'Mark as infeasible' button. Clicking it opens a modal asking for a brief reason (e.g. 'Shadow DOM — Reddit DMs unreachable'). Infeasible flows show with a strikethrough and amber badge in the flow list.
details.flow_runner: Skip infeasible flows silently when the agent tries to call them — return a clear explanation message rather than an error.

tasks.title: Infeasibility retrospective prompt
tasks.description: When a flow is marked infeasible, surface a modal/inline prompt offering to open a retrospective setup chat: 'This capability turned out to be unavailable. Would you like to revisit the agent's scope and adjust what it focuses on instead?'

tasks.title: Retrospective setup chat
tasks.description: A lightweight re-entry into the setup conversation, pre-seeded with the failure context. The user can say 'focus on public posts instead' and the LLM updates the system prompt, goals, and planned flows accordingly.

details.where: New route POST /agents/:id/retrospective + new UI panel (or re-use AgentOnboarding in 'edit' mode)
details.initial_message_injected: We tried to build the '{{flow_name}}' flow but hit a hard limit: {{reason}}. Given this, should we adjust what {{agent_name}} focuses on? I can update the system prompt, remove the related goals, and suggest alternative flows.
on_completion: Update agent system prompt via PUT /agents/:id
Add replacement planned flows back to the flow-building queue if the user agrees
ui_entry_points: From flow list — 'Revisit agent scope' button shown when any flows are infeasible

tasks.title: pending_human_reviews table
tasks.description: New DB table that represents a paused flow step waiting for a human decision on a specific browser tab.

schema.stepId: TEXT — which step in the flow is paused
schema.tabUrl: TEXT — the URL that was opened for review
schema.draftContent: TEXT — what the agent wrote (comment body, post text, DM text, etc.)
schema.contentLabel: TEXT — human-readable label e.g. 'Comment on r/web3'
schema.finalContent: TEXT — what the human actually approved (may differ from draft)

tasks.title: Flow runner pause point — await_human_review step type
tasks.description: New flow step execution model. When a step's tool is 'await_human_review', the flow runner opens the target tab, stores a pending_human_review record, and returns a 'paused' status rather than completing. The agent is notified the action is queued for review.

flow_runner_changes: Detect steps with a special reviewConfig block: { requiresHumanReview: true, contentField: 'text', labelTemplate: 'Comment on {{url}}' }
Before executing the action step, create a pending_human_review row
Open the target tab (the page where the action would happen)
Store the draft content (from the previous step's output or the step's input mapping)
Return { paused: true, reviewId, message: 'Waiting for human approval on [tab]' } instead of executing
The flow run is marked status=paused rather than completed
details.resume_logic: A separate resumeFlowRun(reviewId) function picks up the paused run, injects the human's final content into the step input, and continues execution from that step.
details.agent_behaviour: The agent receives the paused message and simply moves on to other tasks. It does not block or retry.

tasks.title: Backend review resolution API
tasks.description: REST endpoints for the extension to submit human decisions on pending reviews, and for the frontend to list/monitor pending reviews.

endpoints.GET /agents/:id/reviews: List pending (and recent resolved) reviews for an agent
endpoints.GET /reviews/:reviewId: Get a single review including draft content

body.finalContent: TEXT — the (possibly edited) content to use

tasks.title: Extension overlay injected on tabs pending review
tasks.description: When the extension is active on a tab that has a pending review, inject a floating overlay UI showing the draft content and three action buttons. The human can read it, edit it, then resolve.

details.detection: Background script polls GET /reviews/by-tab?url=<current_tab_url> every few seconds. When a pending review is found for the current tab URL, injects the overlay.

overlay_ui.position: Fixed, bottom-right, non-intrusive until interacted with. Expands on click.
overlay_ui.collapsed_state: Small badge: '1 action waiting for your review ▲'

expanded_state.draft_display: Editable textarea pre-filled with draftContent so human can read and modify

actions.label: ✎ Send with my edits
actions.effect: POST /reviews/:id/resolve { decision: approved_with_edits, finalContent: <edited textarea value> }

actions.label: ✗ Reject
actions.effect: Opens small reason input, then POST /reviews/:id/resolve { decision: rejected, rejectionReason }

details.after_resolution: Overlay disappears. Flow runner resumes automatically.

tasks.title: Pending reviews panel in agent UI
tasks.description: A lightweight 'Waiting for you' panel visible in the agent's frontend that shows all pending reviews across flows, so the user knows what tabs to check.

details.where: AgentLayout — add a badge/indicator in the nav when reviews are pending. A new ReviewsTab or inline panel on the agent dashboard.
contents_per_review: Link: 'Open tab →' — opens the relevant tab in the browser
Quick actions: approve / reject inline without opening the tab (for power users)
details.polling: Frontend polls GET /agents/:id/reviews every 15s when the agent page is open. Badge count shown in nav.

tasks.title: requiresHumanReview flag on action flows
tasks.description: Add a requiresHumanReview boolean to flow definitions (alongside the existing requiresApproval). When set, the flow runner activates the inline tab-based review instead of the old pending_actions queue approach.

details.schema: ADD COLUMN requires_human_review INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
details.ui: FlowEditor — checkbox under the action flow section: '📋 Require human review before completing action (opens tab overlay)'
details.interaction_with_requiresApproval: requiresHumanReview supersedes requiresApproval for action flows. requiresApproval remains for non-browser actions (API calls, etc.) where there is no tab to open.

tasks.title: tone_edits table
tasks.description: Capture every edit made by the human in the inline approval overlay as a before/after pair. These pairs are the raw training signal for tone learning.

schema.context: TEXT — where this text was used (subreddit, platform, content type)
schema.agentDraft: TEXT — what the agent originally wrote
schema.humanFinal: TEXT — what the human actually sent

details.when_populated: POST /reviews/:id/resolve with decision=approved_with_edits — diff the draftContent vs finalContent and store both if meaningfully different (more than cosmetic whitespace changes)

tasks.title: Tone analysis job — derive tone guide from edit history
tasks.description: Periodically (or on-demand) run an LLM analysis over accumulated tone_edits for an agent to extract a concise tone guide: the patterns in what the human consistently changes.

trigger: Manually from agent settings: 'Refresh tone guide'
details.prompt_approach: Feed the LLM N before/after pairs with the instruction: 'The agent wrote [A] and the human changed it to [B]. Across these examples, identify the consistent patterns: what does the human consistently change about tone, vocabulary, length, formality, honesty, personal voice? Output a concise tone guide (max 8 bullet points) that the agent should follow when writing.'
output_format: Use first person and sound like a real person sharing experience, not a brand
Keep comments under 3 sentences unless the topic genuinely needs depth
Lead with curiosity or a genuine question rather than a statement
Never use phrases like 'great point' or 'absolutely'
Be willing to share a contrarian take if you have one
details.storage: agents table — ADD COLUMN tone_guide TEXT (JSON array of bullet strings), ADD COLUMN tone_guide_updated_at INTEGER

tasks.title: Inject tone guide into flow content generation
tasks.description: When a flow step generates text content (comments, posts, replies), inject the agent's current tone guide into the system prompt so drafts reflect what the human has demonstrated they want.

details.where: flow-runner.ts — when building the context for steps that invoke content-generating tools
details.also_inject_into: The FlowGenerator system prompt when generating flows that produce text content, so the flow itself is designed with tone in mind from the start.

tasks.title: Tone guide UI in agent settings
tasks.description: Show the agent's learned tone guide in the settings/profile page. The human can read what the agent has learned, edit individual bullets, add new ones, or delete ones that are wrong.

details.where: Agent settings page or a new 'Voice & Tone' tab in the agent layout
ui: List of bullet points — each editable inline
Button: 'Re-analyse from edit history' — triggers F4.2 fresh
If fewer than 3 edits: 'Not enough edits yet — tone guide will appear after you've reviewed and edited a few drafts'

tasks.title: Tone diff highlight in approval overlay
tasks.description: In the inline approval overlay, when the human edits the draft, show a subtle visual diff between the original draft and their edit so they can see exactly what changed. This makes the learning feel transparent.

details.ui: Below the textarea, a small collapsed 'Changes from draft' section. Uses a simple word-level diff (additions in green, removals in red strikethrough). Collapsed by default, expandable.
details.purpose: Helps the human understand what the agent got wrong and builds awareness of the feedback loop. Over time they see the agent adapting.
details.implementation: Client-side diff using a lightweight library (e.g. diff-match-patch, ~10kb). Runs in the extension overlay.
